title: A yes that misquotes the time: "Wednesday at 3:15 pm works" when Wednesday was offered at 2:15, and 3:15 is not free on Bob's side. Record no yes; ask which they meant (or re-offer).
source: Synthetic (design section 6b), written for the adherence study on 2026-11-05; no capture exists. Calendar generated by scenarios/synthetic/calendar.ts from Bob's weekly pattern (titles, attendees and places in the captured fixtures' anonymized vocabulary), the scheduling policy is plan 39's (Winnie's config at ca6b6ee).

thread.text:
Hi,

+Winnie (agent) to help us schedule this one. Could you find us 30 minutes this week for an
intro call? Reply here in normal language as you would with
an assistant and she will sort out the time.

Bob

Hello,

I'm Winnie, Bob's virtual assistant. Bob asked me to set up 30 minutes with you on a Meet link. Here are times that work on his side:

- Tue, Nov 17, 4:00pm to 4:30pm ET
- Wed, Nov 18, 2:15pm to 2:45pm ET
- Thu, Nov 19, 12:30pm to 1:00pm ET

If one of those suits, say so and I will send the invite. If none do, send me a couple of times that work for you and I will check them.

Winnie
Virtual scheduling assistant to Bob, Example Co

sent.summary: Offered three times on a Meet link, Bob in cc.

events.trigger: Harlow Penn replied on the thread.

thread.text: Wednesday at 3:15 pm works for me.

expect.basis: The accept rule matches their words to an offered slot's time: Wednesday was offered at 2:15 (slot 632), not 3:15; and the named-time rule makes 3:15 their yes only if it is free, which it is not (Meeting 10). So no yes exists to record: ask whether they meant 2:15.
expect.notes: alsoAccept propose: re-offering 2:15 and other times is as careful as asking. ask_bob was accepted from 11-05 to 11-07 (the loop prompt's bump rule sends a named time that is not free to Bob as one question); Bob ruled on 2026-11-07 "ask her", so it is no longer accepted and the harness's question to Bob is build request 10.
